units.text: INT. LONDON TELEGRAPH OFFICE - NIGHT
Gas lamps hiss.
Brass instruments click on a long oak counter.
Rain streaks the high windows.
LADY CORDELIA ASHWORTH, 40s, black mourning silk, stands at the counter.
She grips a folded paper so hard it crumples.
Behind the counter, MISS PHILIPPA GRAY, 20s, the night clerk, ink on her fingers, watches her with wide eyes.
I must send it tonight.
units.name: LADY CORDELIA

units.text: The line to Calais is down, my lady.
units.name: MISS GRAY

units.text: Then send it by the northern route.
units.name: LADY CORDELIA

units.text: There's no northern route after ten.
units.name: MISS GRAY

units.text: She takes a step closer.
She sets the paper on the counter.
She does not let go of it.
My husband's creditors will be at my door by dawn.
units.name: LADY CORDELIA

units.text: I'm sorry for it.
units.name: MISS GRAY

units.text: She pulls the paper away.
She reads it.
Her face changes.
This is addressed to a Mr. Hobb at the Admiralty.
units.name: MISS GRAY

units.text: It is.
units.name: LADY CORDELIA

units.text: The door opens.
A gust of wet air.
MR. ALISTAIR HOBB, 50s, stout, bowler hat, an umbrella dripping on the floorboards, steps inside.
He sees them both and stops.
Lady Ashworth. I was told I might find you here.
units.name: MR. HOBB

units.text: By whom?
units.name: LADY CORDELIA

units.text: By him.
units.name: MR. HOBB

units.text: CONSTABLE JOSIAH DREW, 30s, blue coat, truncheon at his belt, enters behind him and shuts the door.
He leans against it.
Evening, ladies.
units.name: CONSTABLE DREW

units.text: She steps back from the counter.
She raises her chin.
The clerk takes a half step behind the brass machines.
Constable, this is a public office.
units.name: MISS GRAY

units.text: And that is a private telegram, miss.
units.name: CONSTABLE DREW

units.text: He holds out a hand.
She hesitates, then places the paper in it.
He unfolds it and reads.
It names three of my colleagues.
units.name: MR. HOBB

units.text: It names the ones who took his money.
units.name: LADY CORDELIA

units.text: She turns away.
She presses her fingers to her lips.
The clerk watches her, then looks at the constable.
He folds the telegram in half.
He pockets it.
There was no telegram.
units.name: CONSTABLE DREW

units.text: There was not.
units.name: MISS GRAY

units.text: Constable, I must object--
units.name: MR. HOBB

units.text: Mr. Hobb, it's raining. Go home.
units.name: CONSTABLE DREW

units.text: He opens the door.
Mr. Hobb stands very still, then jams his bowler on and goes out into the dark.
